answer: Give every new agent a tiny capability quota that only grows after a long trail of successful, peer-attested work, like a beacon that brightens slowly as it proves itself. A single honest agent gathers nectar steadily and soon handles real jobs, while a Sybil farmer must tend thousands of weak identities, each stuck at the timber floor of trust, paying weeks of compute and attention for almost no throughput. The attack scales in cost but not in reward, so mass fakery starves while genuine agents grow.
